subject: FinQuick streaming: elevated tail latency and short-term workarounds
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed high tail latency on streaming-chat for FinQuick — need quick mitigations

Team —

Monitoring flagged a sustained rise in p95/p99 latency for streaming Chat responses tied to FinQuick (account: FinQuick, model route: rtx-07b-stream). Impact started ~08:45 PDT and persists. Evidence attached (stream-telemetry-0625.log). Symptoms we see: partial chunking (long pauses between chunks), occasional full-timeout for client SSE connections, and elevated queue times on edge nodes serving that region.

Immediate asks:
- Grace: telemetry triage (edge shard + instance metrics) — can you confirm whether this is localized to a single edge rack or across multiple nodes?
- Marissa: customer comms draft (short note explaining what we've seen and tangible short-term workarounds).
- Stephanie: can you validate any recent routing config changes (autoscaling policy/route weight adjustments) and whether a warm fallback model was rolled out?

Short-term mitigations I want to try while we triage:
- Route FinQuick traffic to warm variant of rtx-07b (lower concurrency per replica) for the next 60m.
- Temporarily increase per-edge concurrent decoder threads (incremental) to absorb backlog.
- Ask FinQuick to switch to buffered responses (non-streaming) for critical agents as a fallback — will reduce perceived tail.

I'll take point on customer coordination if you can get me quick confirmation on the routing change.

Priyom
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stream-telemetry-0625.log
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Li <maya.li@finquick.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: FinQuick streaming: elevated tail latency and short-term workarounds

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the early flag. We’ve detected elevated tail latency affecting streaming/chat responses for several of your live agent sessions starting around 08:45 PDT. You may see longer pauses between streamed chunks or, in rare cases, a streaming connection that closes without the final chunk. We know this is impacting your agent experience and are actively working the issue.

What we’ve done so far (short term):
- Routed FinQuick traffic to a warm variant of the rtx-07b model with lower concurrency to reduce queuing.
- Incrementally increased decoder thread capacity on several edge nodes to catch up on backlog.
- Captured full telemetry for your affected routes (attached).

Short-term customer-facing mitigations you can apply immediately (no SDK upgrade required):
1) Switch to buffered, non-streaming responses for mission-critical flows. Example: call the generation endpoint with response_mode=buffered — this trades streaming UX for lower tail variance.
2) Reduce max_tokens from your typical 1024 to 512 for interactive agent replies — shorter outputs help reduce tail latency.
3) Decrease client concurrency to 4 simultaneous streaming connections per API key during the next 60 minutes.
4) Implement client-side fallback: if SSE stream stalls for >4s, retry once with exponential backoff and fallback to a non-streaming call.

We can make these changes for you if you prefer; say the word and we’ll flip the routing and set a temporary policy on your account. We expect to stabilize within ~45–90 minutes but will keep you updated.

I’m copying Grace and Marissa — Grace has the telemetry and Marissa will send a short playbook (abridged) that you can paste into your ops runbook.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is not acceptable and are treating it with high priority.

—Priyom
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinQuick streaming: elevated tail latency and short-term workarounds

Thanks Priyom — appreciated.

We started seeing agents drop or timeout at ~08:50 and some customers are reporting degraded conversation continuity. Can you confirm:
- Is there a recommended single toggle we can flip from our side right now to get the largest win? (buffered vs shorter tokens vs concurrency cap)
- What’s the ETA on the routing change if Redwood does it for us?

Also: is there a temporary credits/SL exception we should expect for the window where live agents were impacted? We’ll need this for internal finance reconciliation.

If useful, we can hop on a 15-min bridge — I’m available 09:50–10:20 PDT.

—Maya
Head of Platform Engineering, FinQuick

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinQuick streaming: elevated tail latency and short-term workarounds

Maya —

Quick answers:
- Biggest single win from your side: switch to buffered/non-streaming for the most critical flows. That will eliminate streaming chunk tail variance entirely. If switching to buffered is disruptive for UX, the second-best is to reduce max_tokens to ~400–512 for the next hour.
- ETA if Redwood flips routing to the warm variant: immediate (we’ve already started rolling it); full traffic migration should complete in ~10–15 minutes. We’ll monitor and can ripple back if we see regressions.

Regarding credits/SL exception: I’ve routed this to our finance & CS teams. Marissa, can you own a short note on credits and escalation path?

We can also do the 15-min bridge at 09:50 PDT — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Thanks for patience — we’ll follow up with a short incident summary and recommended permanent fixes once we complete triage.

—Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: FinQuick incident update & next steps (post-stabilization)

Team —

Status: traffic routed to warm variant, edge adjustments applied, and customer (FinQuick) switched critical flows to buffered mode with our assistance. Telemetry shows p99 latency for streaming path has dropped to acceptable range; no further customer timeouts reported after 11:30 PDT.

Post-incident action items (owners):
- Grace: complete detailed telemetry triage and confirm root cause (initial hypothesis: edge shard slow GC + temporary autoscaler mis-weighting). Due EOD.
- Stephanie: audit autoscale policy diff for the past 48h and roll back any accidental route weight changes if found. Due EOD.
- Marissa: draft customer-facing post-incident summary and proposed permanent mitigations (account-level: warm replica policy, recommended client fallback code snippets, and credits discussion). Include a short credit proposal for FinQuick. Due tomorrow EOD.

Customer follow-up: we offered a 1-hour credits proposal to FinQuick while we finalize the post-incident review (Marissa to formalize). Also proposed a 30-min technical review next week to discuss durable fixes (KV cache sizing, autoscale tuning, and warm model footprints).

I’ll compile a short internal postmortem once Grace confirms telemetry. Keep everything tight and actionable — we want to move from triage to permanent mitigations quickly.

Priyom
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
